documents.title: Bambu Filament Technical Data Sheet V1.0: ASA Aero
Bambu ASA Aero Safety Data Sheet SDS20251127B02
Filament guide: printer, nozzle, AMS, build plate and glue compatibility

notes: Mechanical keys hold the TDS X-Y printed-specimen values; the registry has one key per scope, so the Z values (tensile 21 ± 4 MPa, elongation 2.3% ± 0.9%, bending modulus 1220 ± 110 MPa, bending strength 24 ± 3 MPa, impact 3.4 ± 0.5 kJ/m²) are not stored. Density, melting, Vicat and HDT come from the TDS Physical Properties table and sit under material.* / thermal.*, apart from the printed-specimen mechanical.* rows; the TDS does not state the specimen form for density, Vicat and HDT, and their test_condition says so.

TDS facts with no registry key are not stored: Young's modulus (X-Y 2010 ± 260 MPa, Z 1180 ± 210 MPa), melt index 1.56 ± 0.5 g/10 min (210 °C, 2.16 kg), crystallization temperature N/A, heat deflection temperature 85 °C at 0.45 MPa, saturated water absorption rate 0.80% (25 °C, 55% RH), spool material PC+ABS (temperature resistance 90 °C), spool size diameter 200 mm and height 67 mm, printing and storage humidity < 20% RH (sealed, with desiccant), nozzle size 0.4 (Recommended), 0.6, 0.8 mm (see the nozzle relations), bed surface preparation glue (see the glue relation), retraction length 0.8 - 1.4 mm, retraction speed 20 - 40 mm/s, chamber temperature 45 - 60 °C, max overhang angle ~ 70°, max bridging length ~ 40 mm, support material "Turn on", the X1 Series heatbed drying line (90 - 100 °C, 12 h), suggested annealing 80 to 90 °C for 6 to 12 hours (the TDS sentence says "Bambu ASA"), odor ("Odorless"), skin hazards, chemical stability, solubility, chemical resistance, flammability ("Flammable"), combustion products and their odor.
The TDS recommended chamber temperature (45 - 60 °C) is not written to thermal.chamber_temp: that key is a printer capability, not a filament print setting.
The TDS specimens were printed at a nozzle temperature of 225 °C, below the recommended 240 - 280 °C; the mechanical test_condition records it as written.

Composition disagreement left to review: the TDS (p.3) says "acrylonitrile - styrene - acrylate"; the SDS (p.4, section 3) lists "Poly(butyl acrylate-styrene-acrylic acid)" 95-99 % by wt with CAS 141-32-2 (the CAS number of n-butyl acrylate) and an additive 1-5 % by wt. material.type keeps the TDS cell.

SDS facts with no registry key are not stored: product name "Bambu ASA Aero", model "B02-xx", CLP "Not classified", no PBT/vPvB substance, no endocrine disruptors, conditions to avoid ("Avoid fire, elevated temperatures. direct sunlight.") and "Not hazardous goods" for sea (IMDG), DOT, road (ADR/RID) and air (ICAO-TI/IATA) transport. Its section 9 "No data available" for melting point and density does not override the TDS values.

Source disagreements kept for review: bed temperature (TDS 80 - 90 °C vs the material-table wiki's generic ASA 90 - 100 °C); nozzle sizes (TDS 0.4 (Recommended), 0.6, 0.8 mm vs ABS / ASA / PC wiki "Compatible with 0.4 mm nozzle only; other nozzle sizes are not recommended" vs store FAQ excluding hardened steel 0.6 / 0.8 mm and stainless steel 0.2 mm vs the material-table wiki's generic ASA row, all sizes compatible); AMS HT drying time (drying wiki 8 h vs ABS / ASA / PC wiki 12 h); AMS lite (product sources "not compatible" vs the material-table wiki's generic ASA "Compatible" in its combined AMS / AMS lite column). The product TDS values and the product-specific statements are kept.

Textured PEI Plate: the TDS marks it "(Not Recommended)" and the ASA Aero Printing Guide says "Not Recommend to use Textured PEI Plate" (the first layer can stick too hard and tear). Neither a compatible_with nor a not_compatible_with relation is written: the sources call it not recommended, not incompatible.

The material-table wiki has no ASA Aero row; its generic ASA values (nozzle 240 - 280 °C, which agrees with the TDS; bed 90 - 100 °C; oven drying 80 ℃ for 8 h, which agrees) were used only as corroboration or recorded as disagreements.

The foaming tables (ASA Aero Printing Guide, 220 - 280 °C; ABS / ASA / PC wiki, 220 - 270 °C: minimum flow ratio, maximum volumetric expansion ratio, maximum foaming ratio, minimum print density 0.97 - 0.45 g/cm³; test: 0.4 mm nozzle, 80 mm/s, 80 × 10 × 4 mm³) and the recommended flow ratio 0.42 - 0.7 describe printed parts and slicer settings; no registry key holds them and they are not stored.

Marketing prose proves no number: "Only 50%-75% the density of regular ASA prints", "as light as feather", "Tough with Good Impact Resistance", "Ultra-lightweight & Low Density", "Water & UV Resistance" and "Matte Finish For Easy Coloring" (store page) are not stored as values.
Hex: the store page links no Hex Code document for ASA Aero and none was cached, so no published hex is curated for its only colour (White (46100)).

The store page links a "Filament RoHS" certificate (https://store.bblcdn.com/7f9aced52cd84d3aa6262a11c214ad9b.pdf) and the wiki page "Common print quality problems and solutions" (https://wiki.bambulab.com/en/knowledge-sharing/common-print-quality-problem); neither was cached or read, so safety.certifications is neither curated nor marked not_published.
material.diameter_tolerance (± 0.03 mm) is the store page's own row (Product Features › bullet 5); the TDS gives no tolerance, so it is not restated here and not marked not_published.
No in-the-box list: no official packing list exists for this filament (the store page has no What's in the Box section).

The store has no Refill value for ASA Aero (Spool group: "Filament with spool" only), so no spool requirement is recorded. The store FAQ and the ASA Aero Printing Guide say the filament is not food-contact grade and may release styrene at printing temperatures, and the TDS rates the filament "Odorless" while the store FAQ warns of "Pungent and unpleasant odors" during printing; no registry key holds these.
